post.title: Sales boost still possible after festive season?
post.body: Auto industry seems hopeful that sales momentum will continue even after the festive period because of the GST 2.0 changes, according to the SIAM Convention report. They say companies like Maruti and Hyundai expect growth around 7 percent starting from 2026 or 27. If this really kicks in, could mean some relief for people working in sales, supply chain or marketing, since slow months can be tough. But I’m curious, for those of you in auto or related sectors, do you really see this kind of post-festive sales pickup happening on ground? Or is it just optimistic theory?
post.source: SIAM Convention: Auto industry says sales momentum would continue even after festive period because of GST 2.0

comments.text: Honestly I feel it’s not gonna be that easy. GST cuts sound good but affordability is still a big issue for many. Small cars demand dropped for a reason, and I don’t see that changing overnight just because of tax tweaks.

replies.text: Yea exactly, even if prices drop a bit, buyers are scared or don’t have disposable income. It’s not just tax, it’s overall economic confidence.

comments.text: Worked in auto sales this year, the festive season usually does bring a spike, but post festive is always slow. If GST relief is for real, we might gradually see the slow months getting better, fingers crossed!

replies.text: Thanks for sharing your view! It's good to hear from someone on the ground. Do you think companies are actually preparing for this shift or just hoping?

comments.text: GST 2.0 in theory should improve cash flow and lower prices, but implementation will decide if real buyers feel the benefits. Govt needs to push awareness as well, many people just don’t care what tax rates are till it shows in final price tag.

Auto industry saying growth will pick up after 2026? Lol, by then who knows, electric vehicles and other disruption can change the market completely. So hoping for 7% growth sounds like old world thinking to me.

replies.text: Good point about EVs, market’s changing fast. Maybe traditional car sales momentum will matter less over time, but for now a 7% growth still feels like something worth watching.

comments.text: If you work in marketing or sales my advice is use festive season numbers as a way to build pipeline not just rely on orders. Post festive push needs solid follow up cause many customers decide late.
I just hope companies don’t use this GST talk to postpone real deals or discounts. Sometimes feels like marketing buzz more than actual benefit for us customers.

post.title: Maharashtra Reliance deal only for select few jobs?
post.body: 500 jobs from a new Reliance food facility sounds good but not sure how much it really helps most of us. Maharashtra just signed an MoU with Reliance Consumer to build a ₹1,513-cr food and beverage plant in Katol, with plans for big investment in food parks. I’m guessing this might mostly create some managerial and skilled roles, what about those stuck in less skilled sectors? Also, Reliance talks big revenue goals but does that trickle down to better job security or pay for normal employees? Anybody here working or tried applying for such big corporate projects? How was your experience?
post.source: Maharashtra inks MoU with Reliance for ₹1,513-cr food & beverage facility

comments.text: 500 jobs is nothing compared to 40k crore investment. Mostly high level jobs will go to ppl with good degrees, others will just get contract or temporary work. This stuff usually booms big on paper but slow on actual solid hiring.

I had applied to Reliance Consumer once, interview round was okish but never heard back for months. Guess big companies handle so many candidates they just keep on waiting list. If anyone knows inside, how can we get noticed?

replies.text: Try networking on LinkedIn, sometimes personal references help more than just applying online.

comments.text: Achha ji, 500 jobs for few thousand crores investment ka chunaav? Lagta hai Reliance wants to create jobs for their board members only. Baaki sab kaam machine karega.

At least something is happening in Maharashtra food sector. I hope they also give training or skilling programs to local youth so we don't get left behind. Otherwise it’s just another foreign project with jobs going out of reach.

Thanks for replies guys, I also feel like many will get stuck outside this dream unless they are in the right circle. Networking sounds tough when you dont know anyone at all. Would love to hear if anyone got through these big corporate hiring rounds recently and how?

Keep in mind these MoUs usually have local hiring clauses but implementation is always slow. Govt should enforce better transparency on how many local workers are actually hired vs made promises. That’s where policy can help make a difference.

post.title: Trade Talks and GST Changes Got Me Confused
post.body: This whole trade talk with US feels like a rollercoaster no one really trusts. Letters to the Editor in today's papers from Sept 11 2025 discussed India's trade talks with US, GST cuts on renewable energy, and petrol diesel under GST (Letter source). As someone working in finance, these unpredictable policies make planning super tricky, especially with Trump's erratic reputation mentioned in one letter. On the other hand, GST cuts on renewables sound promising for the future but how soon can these changes actually impact our work life? Anyone here dealing with this chaos at their place or has some clarity on how these moves might trickle down to us workers?

Trade talks with Trump? Might as well wait for unicorns to fly. Kuch bhi ho sakta hai, kabhi haan kabhi naa, aise hi tension lete rehte hain sab log.

replies.text: True but national level decisions impact economy and jobs for real, so thoda serious lena bhi zaroori hai. Sarcasm se kuch solve nahi hota bhai.

Trade deal uncertainty can hit sectors like manufacturing and exports hard, matlab hiring freeze ya salary cuts bhi aa sakte hain. Professionals ko apne skills update rakhna chahiye specially in tech and renewables, kyunki wahan growth chances hain.

post.title: US outsourcing tax making us nervous
post.body: This new outsourcing tax proposal from the US feels like a storm brewing. The HIRE Act introduced by Senator Moreno might tax companies more if they hire foreign workers and limit outsourcing deductions, says the news from multiple sources. For those of us working in Indian IT or planning careers here, this could mean fewer projects or tighter budgets from US clients. Also, companies might rethink how they operate their global centers, which doesn't sound so good for job growth. Anyone else feeling insecure about what this means for our future here?
post.source: India's IT sector nervous as US proposes outsourcing tax

comments.text: This feels like a big headache for everyone working in IT. If US firms start paying more tax for outsourcing, they might just cut down on projects or increase the pressure on those of us doing the work here.

replies.text: Exactly yaar, already workload is unpredictable, now this news adds extra tension. Hope companies figure out a way to keep things steady.

comments.text: Honestly, this whole tax thing sounds like politics playing with our careers. I wonder how long these bills stay on paper before anything real happens tho.
We should prepare with upskilling or maybe shifting focus to roles less dependent on US outsourcing. Heard global centers might also start shifting to other countries, so best keep options ready.
Tax battles like this usually drag on for years, so don’t panic. Start looking at smaller firms or domestic clients as backups, just in case those US deals slow down.
Great! Now US just officially hates our cheap labour. Next step: tax us directly or ban our coffees too.

Bill might face lots of legal hurdles cause enforcement at that scale is tricky. But if it passes, yes companies will see big cost rise and might rethink outsourcing strategy. Could lead to more automation too.

replies.text: Automation is scary for jobs but might be the only way forward if taxes hit outsourcing hard.

post.title: New CEO at Swelect Energy, Kya Changes Aayenge?
post.body: Strange timing for a leadership change in Swelect Energy. Arulkumar Shanmugasundaram has taken over as MD and CEO, replacing R Chellappan who will now be Vice-Chairman, according to the news on AmbitionBox. With his 30 years of experience in renewables and tech, I wonder how this will affect internal culture and growth, especially for mid-level folks like us. It’s always a bit nerve wracking when a new MD steps in with big plans—roadmaps might shift, priorities too. Anyone here worked under such leadership changes? How did it impact your day to day and career growth?

post.title: Startups or bust? Students told to hustle hard
post.body: Feels like they are pushing everyone to become entrepreneurs now. At PSG Institute of Management’s Foundation Day, students were told to start businesses or social projects to create jobs, and that Coimbatore could be India's next startup hub, according to recent news. This kinda makes sense with AI and tech opening new doors, but also kinda overwhelming if you’re not from a business background or just want a regular job. I’ve been thinking, how do you even start when everything feels so uncertain and competitive? Anyone here tried jumping into startups while still studying or just after college?
